slides.title: BWRX-300: 2026 Programme Update
slides.subtitle: UK nuclear sector briefing for manufacturing supply chain partners

stats.label: Completed 21 Jan 2026 — fastest UK GDA to date
SGE fleet proposal: 4.2GW across 3 UK sites
SGE investment target; first power sought by 2034
BWRX-300 under construction at Darlington, Canada

milestones.text: GEH submits final tender to Great British Nuclear; Rolls-Royce selected as preferred bidder for Wylfa two months later.
BWRX-300 completes UK GDA Step 2 — 'no fundamental shortfalls' found; fastest two-step GDA engagement completed to date.
Government publishes the new Advanced Nuclear Framework (ANF) — a private-sector route to market for advanced/SMR projects.
SGE submits an ANF application to build 14 BWRX-300 units (4.2GW) across three UK sites, backed by Samsung C&T, Laing O'Rourke, Aecon, Google Cloud and others.
BWRX-300 momentum continues globally (Darlington construction, Poland, Sweden MoUs); UK supply chain MoUs with Sheffield Forgemasters, AtkinsRéalis, Jacobs and others.

slides.what_it_means: The 'no UK pathway' story has just changed: SGE's 14-unit, 4.2GW proposal is a concrete, privately financed UK route for the BWRX-300 — filed under the new Advanced Nuclear Framework rather than the GBN competition GEH lost. A parallel route to market alongside Rolls-Royce and Holtec.

slides.title: SMR-300: 2026 Programme Update
slides.subtitle: UK nuclear sector briefing for F4N cohort July 2026

stats.label: UK GDA passed — no fundamental shortfalls
UK content target for factory build

milestones.text: US NRC accepts Holtec's Pioneer 1 & 2 Construction Permit Application for review (Palisades, Michigan). Safety/environmental review due early-mid 2027.
SMR-300 completes Step 2 of the UK GDA. No fundamental shortfalls across 21 technical areas; 14 regulatory observations to resolve.
Holtec and EDF Energy sign Heads of Terms for a JV and jointly submit a proposal for up to four SMR-300 units at the former Cottam coal site.
Cottam proposal confirmed: ~1.3GW capacity, targeting power for co-located data centres. Holtec signals plans for a larger UK operations centre.

slides.what_it_means: A second live UK SMR pipeline alongside Wylfa: South Yorkshire (factory) plus Cottam (deployment site). More entry points beyond Rolls-Royce. The 70% UK-content ambition for the factory build offers direct manufacturing opportunity for qualified UK suppliers.

slides.title: PWR-20: 2026 Programme Update
slides.subtitle: UK nuclear sector briefing for F4N cohort July 2026

stats.label: First UK developer to complete Preliminary Design Review

milestones.text: PWR-20 completes the UK's first-ever Preliminary Design Review; ONR says a December 2027 site licence decision remains achievable.
MoU signed with DP World for an £80m, subsidy-free micro-nuclear plant at London Gateway (Thames Freeport, Essex). Targeting operation in 2030.
Closes an oversubscribed third major round of investment of $100m+, led by Astera Institute.
Last Energy UK notifies Welsh Government of intent to submit a Significant Infrastructure Project application for the 4-unit Llynfi (Bridgend) project; formal application expected July 2026.

slides.what_it_means: A fundamentally different model: no government competition to win. Last Energy builds, owns and operates plants, selling power directly to industrial customers on-site, entirely privately financed. Two active UK sites now (London Gateway and Llynfi) with a licensing milestone due December 2027.

slides.title: LFR-AS-200: UK Programme Update
slides.subtitle: UK nuclear sector briefing for F4N cohort July 2026

milestones.text: Newcleo relocates its holding HQ from London to Paris, citing focus on its European precursor and prototype reactor programme.
LFR-AS-200 becomes the first Advanced Modular Reactor design accepted into the UK's Generic Design Assessment — achieved without public funding.
Newcleo announces suspension of its UK reactor development programme, citing lack of access to the UK's plutonium stockpile and insufficient government support.
Closes a further €75m funding round; continues to prioritise Italy, France and Slovakia over the UK for near-term deployment.

slides.what_it_means: A genuine cautionary tale: even a vendor that hit a real UK regulatory first (first AMR into GDA, no public funding needed) pulled back when policy support didn't follow. GDA entry is necessary but not sufficient for UK deployment.

slides.title: Rolls-Royce SMR: 2026 Programme Update
slides.subtitle: UK nuclear sector briefing for F4N cohort July 2026

milestones.text: Yokogawa Electric appointed to supply control systems (Runcorn design facility).
Contract signed with GBE-N for site-specific design at Wylfa; long lead-time equipment ordering begins.
Early Works Contract signed with CEZ Group for Czech Republic's first SMR at Temelín (up to 3GW).
Škoda JS and Doosan Enerbility appointed as dual suppliers for nuclear island components.
Selected by Videberg Kraft (Vattenfall) to deliver 3 SMRs at Värö Peninsula, Sweden — third European contract win.
Pioneer Works manufacturing development centre announced for Derby — precision assembly, welding & testing, ~40 skilled roles.

slides.what_it_means: Only supplier with multiple signed SMR contracts in Europe (UK, Czechia, Sweden). Programme momentum is real, not speculative. Overseas nuclear-island awards (Škoda JS, Doosan) show the 70% UK-content ambition will require active supplier qualification to win work.

slides.title: AP300: 2026 Programme Update
slides.subtitle: UK nuclear sector briefing for F4N cohort July 2026

stats.label: Private AP300 fleet planned, North Teesside
UK GDA complete; Step 2 assessment ongoing

milestones.text: Westinghouse withdraws from Great British Nuclear's SMR competition; Rolls-Royce selected as preferred UK partner two months later.
Six UK supplier MoUs signed (William Cook, Trillium Flow, Curtiss-Wright UK, Boccard UK, Bendalls Engineering, Sheffield Forgemasters).
Springfields, Lancashire marks 80 years as the world's oldest continuously operating nuclear fuel manufacturing site.
AP300 remains in UK 2-step GDA (Step 1 complete). Community Nuclear Power continues developing the privately financed 4-unit fleet at North Teesside, targeting a licensed site by 2027.

slides.what_it_means: Unlike Rolls-Royce, Holtec and X-energy, Westinghouse is not part of the government-backed Wylfa programme. Its UK SMR future rests on the privately financed Teesside project — a different risk profile, potentially faster to market without government procurement timelines.

slides.title: Xe-100: 2026 Programme Update
slides.subtitle: UK nuclear sector briefing for F4N cohort July 2026

milestones.text: US NRC approves the TX-1 fuel facility's Part 70 licence for TRISO-X fuel handling — first Category II licence ever issued.
UK Government confirms Future Nuclear Enabling Fund award (£6.68m); Kier Group joins as UK constructability and supply chain partner.
X-energy lists on Nasdaq (ticker: XE), raising over $1bn — the largest nuclear IPO on record.
Xe-100 HTGR formally submitted into the UK Generic Design Assessment (GDA). Regulatory review expected to conclude by end of 2029.
Closes $700m Series D: $1.4bn raised in a year, $1.8bn total; 144 SMR orders logged globally (11GW).

slides.what_it_means: Earliest-stage UK programme: GDA only just submitted, not expected to conclude until end-2029. Longer runway to prepare, but least near-term certainty. The Xe-100 is a helium-cooled, graphite-moderated HTGR — different technology and supply chain from PWR-based SMRs.

slides.title: STEP Fusion: 2026 Programme Update
slides.subtitle: UK nuclear sector briefing for manufacturing supply chain partners

stats.label: Government funding for STEP via UK Fusion Energy
Tokamak Energy magnets contract to March 2029
Peak construction jobs expected at West Burton

milestones.text: First public consultation on STEP Fusion's DCO held across North Nottinghamshire, Lincolnshire and South Yorkshire communities.
ILIOS consortium (Kier-Nuvia JV, with AECOM, AL_A and Turner & Townsend) appointed Construction Partner — £200m initial contract, up to 8,000 jobs at peak.
UKAEA completes first phase of West Burton site acquisition from EDF — land transferred 3.5 years ahead of schedule.
Tokamak Energy named Magnet Systems Partner — £70m contract to March 2029, securing UK sovereign HTS magnet capability.
At Fusion Fest 2026, UK Fusion Energy and UKAEA launch strategies to 2030/2040; £30m Dassault Systèmes digital/PLM deal signed.

slides.what_it_means: STEP is a single UK national programme, not a multi-vendor competition — the entry point is UKFE's own procurement portal. Already a live, spending programme with £108.8m industry contracts placed and site construction starting. Earlier in spend terms than most SMR programmes.

slides.title: Decommissioning Programmes: 2026 Update
slides.subtitle: UK nuclear sector briefing for manufacturing supply chain partners

stats.label: NDA group's annual supply chain spend
SME win: LTi Metaltech, Sellafield SRP, Feb 2026
Hunterston B & Hinkley Pt B transfer to NDA in 2026

milestones.text: Three companies win contracts worth up to £2.9bn for non-nuclear infrastructure works at Sellafield — context for the scale of work entering the market.
Sellafield awards a £45m contract to LTi Metaltech to supply plutonium storage containers ('100-year cans') for the new Product and Residue Store Retreatment Plant.
NDA publishes its latest group Strategy, effective March 2026 — a refreshed roadmap prioritising hazard reduction and collaboration.
Hunterston B becomes the first AGR site to transfer from EDF Energy to the NDA group for decommissioning, with Hinkley Point B to follow.
Sellafield's PPP marks 7 years, with major projects (SRP, SIXEP Continuity Plant, BEPPS2, LSS1) progressing through construction and design.

slides.what_it_means: The largest, steadiest source of UK nuclear manufacturing demand in this briefing — £1.8bn spent every year, for decades, regardless of how any single SMR programme fares. LTi Metaltech's £45m win shows UK SMEs can secure significant contracts in this market.

slides.title: UK Nuclear Submarine Fleet: 2026 Update
slides.subtitle: UK nuclear sector briefing for manufacturing supply chain partners

stats.label: UK jobs supported at peak production

milestones.text: UK and Australia sign the Geelong Treaty — a 50-year bilateral agreement governing joint construction of Australia's SSN-AUKUS submarines.
HMS Anson becomes the first RN nuclear submarine to undergo a maintenance period in Australia, at HMAS Stirling.
Australia announces A$310m payment to the UK for long-lead reactor items; manufacture of complete welded nuclear propulsion systems begins at Rolls-Royce Submarines, Derby.
Australian Submarine Supplier Qualification programme expanded to link Australian businesses into UK submarine supply chains for the first time.
UK Parliament's Defence Committee warns of 'shortcomings and failings', flagging delays to the Barrow shipyard upgrade and submarine availability as 'critically low'.
Defence Secretary John Healey confirms four PWR3+ reactors are under construction at the expanded Rolls-Royce Raynesway facility in Derby.

slides.what_it_means: The largest sustained nuclear manufacturing programme in this briefing — up to 12 boats, one every 18 months, 21,000 jobs at peak, with billions already committed to Barrow and Derby. Entry requires ITAR clearance and strict quality regimes, but the pipeline is multi-decade and real.
